annotations.title: Is this artwork in the catalog? (title from memory, artist, description)

description: ONE call that says whether a work is in our catalog, for a visitor who cannot name it exactly: a half-remembered or translated title, an artist, a description of the picture — or several of them. It matches the title words against EVERY work of the artist (not only 10 search results) and runs the full-text search in the visitor's language and English; a description goes through the meaning index. Returns verdict ("found", "candidates", "possible_matches_by_meaning", "artist_works_listed" or "not_in_catalog"), next_step (what to do now — follow it), candidates (at most 5, best first: pk, artist_name, title, year, url, image_url), and, when an artist was recognised, artist (pk, url, artworks_count, all_artworks_page) and artist_works (the titles of his works, to spot the same work under another title). Use it FIRST, instead of a series of search_artworks with title variants. When you learn the work's real title (from the encyclopedia or the visitor), call it once more with alternative_titles; after that, do not search again.

alternative_titles.description: Other titles of the same work: the English title, the real title found in the encyclopedia (e.g. "Pêcheur à la coquille" for "le sourire napolitain").

artist.description: Artist name, when the visitor gave one.

description.description: What the picture shows, when the visitor describes it.

language.description: Site language code (2 letters, e.g. "en", "fr"). Default "en".

title.description: The title as the visitor gave it (from memory, any language).
